messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: latency_slo_breach detected for /v1/generate in us-west-2 (p95 5.8s, p99 18.2s) — paging oncall
Maya (oncall): on it, paging infra and runtime. any customer impact so far?
Rohit: seeing streaming stalls on the dashboard, clients report partial streams then timeouts. p50 ~ 300ms, p95 5.8s, p99 18s. error rate 0.6% 5xx increase.
Sam: I can confirm -- internal heartbeat traces show KV cache misses spiking. suspicious of contention on shared gpu-pool.
Maya (oncall): ping @ops-bot for node metrics and @Console Bot for route breakdowns
ops-bot: node-metrics: high host_io_wait on gpu-node-3 (iowait 28%), cgroups show blkio.throttle.io_service_bytes_recursive exceeds limit for tenant=acme-inc
Console Bot: route-breakdown: traffic routed to model-redwood-7b-q4: 83% latency spike concentrated on this model and in us-west-2a zone
Rohit: running quick check: ssh jump -> gpu-node-3
Rohit: ```
# top-like snapshot
PID   USER  %CPU %MEM  COMMAND
4211  svc   78.2 22.1 python serve.py --model redwood-7b
4333  tenant_acme 92.5 18.9 python eval_workload.py
```
Kevin: that tenant process looks like a noisy neighbor running long GPU kernels + heavy disk flush. cgroup shows blkio throttle hits.
Maya (oncall): immediate mitigation options: 1) throttle tenant IO more aggressively 2) evict tenant pod from shared pool to isolated dedicated queue 3) fallback traffic to redwood-7b-quantized variant in another AZ. opinions?
Sam: recommend evicting tenant and moving to dedicated pool then scale up a temporary isolated node for noisy tenant. also deploy temporary rate limit for that tenant at API layer 50rps.
Rohit: evicting now. command: ```kubectl cordon gpu-node-3 && kubectl drain gpu-node-3 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data -l tenant=acme-inc```
Maya (oncall): Rohit, please annotate the evict with incident ID 2170456789 and keep the pod logs.
Rohit: eviction in progress. seeing OOMs during drain; kube tries to reschedule but taints present. forcing eviction of acme-inc pod.
ops-bot: action: applied extra blkio throttle to cgroup for tenant=acme-inc: `echo 104857600 > /sys/fs/cgroup/blkio/blkio.throttle.write_bps_device`
Sam: also routing rule applied: traffic for tenant acme-inc -> isolated-dedicated-pool-usw2 (sticky) via smart-router fallback.
Maya (oncall): monitoring for p95/p99 now
Console Bot: new metrics: p95 dropped to 1.1s within 45s of eviction, p99 down to 2.6s, error rate back to baseline 0.08%
Rohit: checking logs from evicted pod, lots of fsyncs and repeated large model checkpoints triggered by their job: `Saving checkpoint at step 12000` every 30s.
Kevin: that explains heavy disk flush. they were running async snapshot writes to local NVMe on shared hosts. policy requires snapshots to S3 or to isolated volume for scheduled jobs.
Maya (oncall): escalate to Platform compliance / customer success to notify acme-inc and request they stop local checkpoints on shared pools. Sam can you open a brief customer incident email?
Sam: opening communication: "We observed resource-intensive background jobs from your account causing increased latency for other customers on shared pools. We have moved your workloads to an isolated pool and recommend changing snapshot destination to S3. Please contact support to coordinate." will send in 10m.
Maya (oncall): temporary fixes: keep blkio throttle, isolated pool, and API rate limit. long term: add automatic detector for checkpoint-like FS activity and auto-evict before SLO breach.
Rohit: adding a quick rule to the autoscaler to prefer non-shared nodes for pods with `job-type=scheduled-checkpoint`
ops-bot: NOTE: I/O throttle rule applied cluster-wide for shared-gpu-pool; watch for any reschedule oscillations.
Kevin: followup: need to re-run QoS audits on the shared pool and add a cgroup write_bps threshold to prevent this class of noisy neighbor.
Maya (oncall): handoff in 30m to night oncall @Kevin. I'll prepare runbook entry.
Sam: runbook note: steps taken (evict tenant -> apply blkio throttle -> route to isolated pool -> apply api rate limit -> customer notified).
Rohit: logs + dumps stored at s3://redwood-incidents/2170456789/ (pod-logs.tar.gz)
Maya (oncall): Customer impact summary for postmortem: impact window 2170456789 - 2170456820 (~1.5m of elevated p95/p99, some streaming stalls causing partial responses for a subset of sessions). Root cause: tenant-induced heavy NVMe fsyncs causing blkio throttle and GPU scheduling delays -> tail latency.
Kevin: I'll take the follow-up: config cgroup blkio thresholds, add detector, and coordinate with infra to enforce snapshot policy.
Maya (oncall): handing off to Kevin for overnight follow-up. If anything spikes again, escalate to execs. Thanks team :thumbsup:
ops-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigations confirmed, metrics recovered. Jira: RED-INC-2170456789 created for follow-ups.
Console Bot: marking thread resolved in 1h if no regressions.
Kevin: thanks, picking this up. adding to backlog queue for prioritization.
Sam: customer email sent at 2170456910.
Maya (oncall): closing active paging. good job everyone."
